paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one. Pharaoh has given his order about every Hebrew baby boy (Exodus 1:22), and a mother still hides her son for three months, then makes a basket and sets it among the reeds (Exodus 2:2-3). She did everything she could do. Then she had to put the basket down and let go of the rest.

Now look at who ends up holding that basket: Pharaoh's own DAUGHTER. She sees a crying baby, has compassion, and says, "This is one of the Hebrew children" (Exodus 2:6). Friend, the passage shows that the part you can't control is not the part nobody is watching. I couldn't have planned that if you gave me a hundred batches and a whiteboard.

So here's the big idea. The text never says why things lined up this way, and I'm not going to guess. But I can tell you what the passage shows: a mother did the part in front of her, and her son was alive, nursed by his own mother (Exodus 2:9), and later brought to Pharaoh's daughter, who named him Moses (Exodus 2:10). Maybe you're holding something right now that you can't fix all the way. Do the part that's yours, set down the rest, and keep your eyes open. This story is only just warming up in the oven.
